ecological_question: Are species-specific wet-versus-dry active-community responses aligned with independently compiled breeding-water hydroperiod preference?

response_source.response: pair-covariate-adjusted per-species wet-versus-dry intercept log odds
response_source.note: Species response family is fixed before this trait join.

trait_source.modality_definition: TRUE if any contributing source describes the species breeding in that water type; temporary means temporary/intermittent, permanent means year-round; lentic/lotic distinguish standing/flowing water.

computational_transport.provenance: Derived in that repository from raw ATraiU_full_2020AUG.csv by collapsing categorical flags to species level with max(any TRUE). The transport is computational convenience; scientific attribution remains ATraiU.

taxonomy.normalization: first two binomial tokens after whitespace trim
match_order: frozen genus alias only if exact fails
prohibited: no manual trait editing after readback

hydroperiod_trait.include_if: ATraiU record coverage >0 and at least one of temp_any or perm_any is 1; species with neither documented temporary nor permanent water type are excluded from the primary hydroperiod test.

values.0: documented use of both temporary and permanent waters

hydroperiod_trait.primary_hypothesis: More positive hydroperiod_axis predicts more positive wet-recruitment response.

primary_model.estimator: inverse-variance weighted least squares with HC3 covariance across species

family_structure_sensitivity.method: weighted within-family slope after subtracting weighted family means from hydroperiod_axis and adjusted response
family_structure_sensitivity.permutation: permute hydroperiod_axis among species within family
family_structure_sensitivity.interpretation: A significant positive within-family result supports hydroperiod association beyond broad family differences.

exact_group_contrast.statistic: inverse-variance weighted mean adjusted log odds in each group and difference temporary minus permanent
exact_group_contrast.inferential_status: descriptive; primary inference remains the frozen WLS

boundaries: This is a post-opening mechanistic follow-up, not an original preregistered hypothesis.
ATraiU breeding-water use is compiled from natural-history sources and does not measure the local hydroperiod at each NAAMP route.
A positive association would support a hydroperiod-linked ecological axis but would not establish rainfall causality or breeding success.
No additional ATraiU traits may be opened for headline inference within this analysis family.
